integrity_rule: Team macro intelligence is append-oriented. Source facts, MAYHEM inference, conflicts and post-match validation remain separately identifiable. Stale observations must not be presented as current without a new capture.

evidence.fact: Leka Halasima withdrew from Round 27 with an ankle injury and is expected to be available for week one of the finals.
Wayde Egan and Kurt Capewell are being rested for Round 27.
Taine Tuaupiki is listed at fullback and Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad shifts into the centres in the late-mail configuration.
Warriors entered Round 27 in 1st position and were chasing the minor premiership.

Warriors.macro_inference: High-end season position is intact, but Round 27 carries deliberate rotation plus a forced backline change. This is a continuity cost rather than evidence of broad team deterioration.

evidence.fact: Sea Eagles entered Round 27 in 9th position and were out of finals contention.
The same 19-man squad used against the Dragons was retained for the Warriors match.
Manly scored 44 points in consecutive wins over the Dragons and Knights immediately before Round 27.

Sea Eagles.macro_inference: Eliminated from finals but carrying strong recent attacking form and lineup continuity, making them a materially stronger spoiler profile than ladder position alone suggests.

evidence.fact: Cowboys entered Round 27 in 8th position with a finals berth secured.
Tom Dearden returned from injury in the Round 26 win and remained at halfback for Round 27.
Robert Derby was named on the wing for Round 27.

Cowboys.macro_inference: Finals qualification reduces existential stakes but Dearden's return improves spine continuity. Round 27 remains a momentum and combination-quality test rather than a qualification game.

evidence.fact: Raiders entered Round 27 in 12th position.
Coby Black was named at halfback for his NRL debut.
Josh Papalii was approaching retirement and Round 27 formed part of Canberra's season-ending farewell context.

Raiders.macro_inference: No finals pressure, but a debuting half and farewell context increase uncertainty around normal late-season baseline behaviour.

evidence.fact: Sharks entered Round 27 in 5th position.
Cronulla entered the match after a 38-18 loss to Parramatta.
Riley Pollard and Niwhai Puru were named in the halves, with Riley Jones and Michael Gabrael in the centres.

Sharks.macro_inference: Finals-bound but entering Round 27 with significant combination disruption in key decision-making and outside-back roles. Current form/continuity risk is elevated relative to ladder position.

evidence.fact: Storm entered Round 27 in 11th position and were missing finals for the first time in 16 years.
Melbourne entered Round 27 after a large win over Brisbane.
Cameron Munster, Jahrome Hughes and Harry Grant were named in the Round 27 spine/core lineup.

Storm.macro_inference: Ladder outcome is poor by club standards, but the Round 27 side retains elite core playmaking continuity and arrives off a strong performance. Season position alone understates immediate-match capability.

evidence.fact: Blake Lawrie comes into the starting side at prop, Loko Pasifiki Tonga moves to lock and Ryan Couchman moves to the bench for Round 27.
Kyle Flanagan and Lyhkan King-Togia were named in the halves for Round 27.

Dragons.macro_inference: The main current structural change is through the middle rotation rather than the halves. No broader team-level conclusion is justified without further evidence.

evidence.fact: Jordan Samrani returns in the centres, moving Sean Russell to the interchange.
Jack de Belin returns on the bench after three NSW Cup games.
Tyrese Lokeni is in line for his NRL debut.
Mitchell Moses and Ronald Volkman were named in the halves.

Eels.macro_inference: Parramatta carry improving personnel depth into the final round, while the first-grade debut element adds some bench uncertainty. Spine continuity remains comparatively strong.

evidence.fact: Panthers entered Round 27 in 2nd position on 40 competition points with a +308 differential.
Mitch Kenny returned from a leg injury and started at hooker in Round 27.
Isaah Yeo was elevated to the interchange after three games out and returned in Round 27.
Official NRL post-match reporting confirms both Yeo and Kenny successfully returned as Penrith beat Wests Tigers 38-10 and secured the 2026 minor premiership.
Luke Garner started at centre for Izack Tago, who was out with a knee injury in Round 27.

Panthers.macro_inference: Penrith enter Finals Week One as minor premiers with the prior Yeo participation uncertainty resolved and both Yeo and Kenny having completed first-grade returns. That improves evidenced core-role availability relative to the pre-Round-27 state, but Finals Week One selection, workload and any performance uplift remain unconfirmed until official team lists and checkpoint evidence.

evidence.fact: Latu Fainu returns on the interchange after a hamstring injury.
Vaka Aho is named to make his NRL debut from the bench.
Sione Fainu replaces Tony Sukkar, who has delayed concussion symptoms.
Sunia Turuva is listed on the bench after missing two games with a knee injury.

Wests Tigers.macro_inference: Multiple return/debut elements increase bench and rotation variability. The team profile contains more personnel-transition uncertainty than a settled late-season lineup.
